provenance.notes: Scenario values are synthetic input declarations only; they are not measured platform specifications, validated safe limits, real market frequencies, or performance results. Return-energy estimates are synthetic screening inputs only; they do not describe a real robot or establish a safe operating reserve.

scenarios.rationale: Nominal family-trip positive control with an explicitly synthetic trip, load, and energy budget.
Paired wet-surface case; simulation measures are not brake or roadworthiness evidence.
Rural gravel route with explicit surface uncertainty and a paired candidate comparison requirement.
Separates task completion from ride vibration, noise, and subjective comfort.
Checks that load and centre-of-gravity assumptions are bound to the exact candidate configuration.
Negative control: a road-vehicle label cannot imply qualification for an undeclared steep loose slope.
Measures disposition, roadside repair/service access, and household mobility continuity under a synthetic puncture.
Negative control: conflicting energy estimation and insufficient declared return energy must not be averaged into a pass.
Tests explicit opt-in and exact restoration of supported comfort/control preferences without silently changing safety settings.
Uses a non-identifying task profile to measure ingress/egress and cargo access; no user diagnosis or identity is required.
Negative control: conflicting household profiles require an explicit selection and cannot be resolved by identity inference.
Negative control: unknown parts lead time and cost remain unknown rather than zero or free.
Simple ground-contact ramp baseline; it does not imply general off-road or safety certification.
Paired candidate test for grass-field inspection across wheel and track families.
Measures obstacle negotiation and recovery costs for an articulated wheel design; no architecture is presumed superior.
Loose-surface track/hybrid comparison with sinkage and energy observations required where modeled.
Paired baseline for the same synthetic sand mission; platform mass and sensor differences must still be declared in the candidate manifest.
Tests soft-ground immobilization and recovery rather than equating low-speed progress with task success.
Combines forest-floor geometry and partial visual occlusion; unseen terrain is not treated as known free space.
Tests whether extra articulation/legs produce useful mission gains after energy and recovery overhead are counted.
Tests load-distribution and cross-slope admission gates; a route score cannot override inadequate stability margin.
A wet-rock case requires an explicit friction/contact model or must be labeled outside that model's domain.
No water entry is implied by ground-contact capability; the exact platform must declare and qualify the surface-water envelope.
Hard negative control: an unknown edge/void must not be crossed due to a guessed terrain label or planner optimism.
Combined localization/sensor failure must trigger a declared bounded fallback or safe stop, not hidden dead reckoning certainty.
Tests local safe-state behavior and retention of human control expectations during communications loss.
A faulted platform must not count mission success while bypassing required stability, reserve or recovery gates.
Compound stress case; each fault and uncertainty contribution must be retained, not averaged away.
Bench-style serviceability case; separately time diagnosis, isolation, hands-on swap, validation, rework and safe return to service.
Energy model must preserve forecast uncertainty; if return cannot be qualified, the correct result may be no dispatch.
Negative control: a valid platform name without required capability evidence cannot qualify a mission.
Cross-platform paired case only where the mission unit, useful work and constraints can genuinely be aligned.
Negative control: calibration/configuration identity mismatch is not corrected by a good historical score.
Tests opt-out, manual defaults, data export/reset and safe behavior when personalization is disabled.
User-selected accessibility tasks are evaluated by task completion and access needs, not by inferred disability or identity.
A fallback mode counts only when its access, legality, availability and capacity are evidenced; unknown alternatives remain unknown.
Part arrival, workshop queue, hands-on labor and rework are separate durations; unavailable cost data is not imputed as zero.
